chapterNote: The traveler's psalm, second of the Songs of Ascents that pilgrims sang on the climb to Jerusalem. It opens with eyes lifted to the hills and an honest question — where is my help going to come from? — for the hills held both the destination and the dangers: bandits, heat, ravines, the shrines of other gods on their high places. The answer overshoots every hill: my help comes from the LORD, Maker of heaven and earth. From there the psalm hands the traveler over to his Keeper, and the keeping-word, shamar, tolls six times in eight verses: He will not let your foot slip; He never dozes at the watch — behold, the Keeper of Israel neither slumbers nor sleeps; He is your shade at your right hand against sun by day and moon by night. The last pair of verses widens the escort to everything: the LORD will keep you from all evil, He will keep your soul, He will keep your going out and your coming in, from now to forever. It is the psalm parents pray over departing children and the church prays over its dead — every journey, and the journey, under the same unsleeping watch.

1.text: A song of ascents. I lift up my eyes to the hills. From where will my help come?
1.amp: A Song [shir] of degrees [maaloth — of ascents, the pilgrim climb]. I will lift up [nasa] my eyes [ayin] unto the hills [har], from whence comes my help [ezer]? ['Shall I lift up mine eyes to the hills? whence should my help come?', the KJV margin]
1.notes: The maaloth (H4609) are the ascents: the climbing road to Jerusalem. The hills hold promise and peril at once — the city ahead, the bandits and high-place shrines between — so the lifted ayin (H5869) ends in a real question: meayin, from where, does ezer (H5828) come? Not from the hills themselves.

2.text: My help comes from the LORD, who made the heavens and the earth.
2.amp: My help [ezer] comes from the LORD [YHWH], which made [asah] heaven [shamayim] and earth [eretz].
2.notes: The answer overshoots the hills entirely: help from the One who asah (H6213) the shamayim the hills stand under and the eretz they stand on. The Maker-title is the Ascents' recurring credential (cf. Psalm 124:8) — competence proven at creation scale, applied to one traveler's road.

3.text: He will not let your foot be shaken loose; your Keeper does not drowse.
3.amp: He will not suffer [natan — allow] your foot [regel] to be moved [mot — to slip, totter]: He that keeps [shamar] you will not slumber [num — doze, nod off].
3.notes: The psalm turns and addresses the traveler — another voice, or faith answering its own question. mot (H4132) is the slip on the scree the climber fears most, and shamar (H8104), the watchman's verb, begins its six-fold toll. num (H5123): the Watchman does not even nod.

4.text: Look — the Keeper of Israel neither drowses nor sleeps.
4.amp: Behold, He that keeps [shamar] Israel [Yisrael] shall neither slumber [num] nor sleep [yashen].
4.notes: The personal guard is also the national one: the shomer of one pilgrim keeps all Yisrael, and the negation doubles — neither num nor yashen (H3462), not the doze nor the deep sleep. Baal's prophets had to scream to wake their god (cf. 1 Kings 18:27); Israel's Keeper has no closing time.

5.text: The LORD Himself is your Keeper; the LORD is the shade at your right hand.
5.amp: The LORD [YHWH] is your keeper [shamar]: the LORD is your shade [tsel] upon your right [yamin] hand [yad].
5.notes: The center of the psalm, and its creed: YHWH shomrekha, the LORD your Keeper. The tsel (H6738) at the yamin (H3225) is the shadow that walks with the traveler on the sun-hammered road — protection positioned at the working hand, close as your own side (cf. Isaiah 25:4).

6.text: By day the sun will not strike you down, nor the moon by night.
6.amp: The sun [shemesh] shall not smite [nakah] you by day [yomam], nor the moon [yareach] by night [layil].
6.notes: nakah (H5221) is the striking-verb of real blows: sunstroke on the exposed climb, and the night's own dangers under the yareach (H3394) — cold, and every ancient dread the moon carried. Day-shift and night-shift both covered; the Keeper works around the clock He made.

7.text: The LORD will keep you from all evil; He will keep your very soul.
7.amp: The LORD [YHWH] shall preserve [shamar] you from all [kol] evil [ra]: He shall preserve [shamar] your soul [nephesh].
7.notes: The keeping widens past sunstroke to kol ra (H7451), all evil — and deepens past circumstances to the nephesh (H5315) itself. Bodies still meet hardship on the road; the soul under this shamar is beyond reach (cf. Matthew 10:28; John 10:28).

8.text: The LORD will keep your going out and your coming home, from this moment on and forever.
8.amp: The LORD [YHWH] shall preserve [shamar] your going out [yatsa] and your coming in [bo] from this time forth, and even for [ad] evermore [olam].
8.notes: The sixth and final shamar covers the whole grammar of a life: yatsa and bo (H3318, H935), every departure and every homecoming, the day's errands and the last journey both. And the term of the watch: me-attah ve-ad olam (H5704, H5769) — from now, without end. The pilgrim may sleep; his Keeper never will.
